findings.title: Large CAD layers are silently processed only partially
findings.body: When more than 4,500 horizontal lines exist, the parser keeps an arbitrary first 4,500 based on Revit geometry enumeration order and silently discards the rest. Valid foundation outlines can therefore be omitted or cut in half. If any earlier outline remains placeable, the command still commits and reports success, leaving the user with an incomplete foundation layout and no warning. The input limit should be enforced per extraction group with an explicit failure, or all geometry should be processed using a bounded strategy that does not discard valid lines.

findings.title: Core contracts unnecessarily require the Revit API
findings.body: This interface imports Autodesk.Revit.DB even though its public contract uses only object, FoundationData, and List<T>; FoundationPlacementOrchestrator has the same unused import. Consequently, compiling Antigravity.Core now requires Autodesk.Revit.DB namespace resolution despite the adapter/parser abstractions exposing no Revit types. In builds where Core intentionally lacks a Revit assembly reference, AC-02 fails with CS0234/CS0246. Remove both unused Autodesk imports, or explicitly make Revit types part of the contract and add the required project reference.

findings.title: Unsupported family parameters terminate placement instead of returning failure
findings.body: The newly duplicated type's Length and Width parameters are used without checking StorageType or IsReadOnly. LookupParameter can resolve a non-double or formula/read-only parameter, in which case Parameter.Set(double) throws rather than returning false. This escapes TryGetOrCreateFoundationType and can abort the entire CAD placement transaction instead of letting the orchestrator skip that foundation. Validate both parameters are writable doubles and handle Revit parameter-setting failures under the method's try-style contract.

findings.title: Level selection depends on unspecified input ordering
findings.body: LastOrDefault(l => l.Elevation <= z) does not select the nearest level below z unless the supplied list happens to be sorted by ascending elevation; the fallback FirstOrDefault likewise does not reliably select the lowest level. Revit collector/list ordering is not guaranteed by this constructor contract, so a foundation can silently be associated with the wrong level. Select the matching candidate explicitly by elevation (maximum elevation at or below z, with a deterministic nearest-level fallback).

findings.title: Level selection depends on unspecified input ordering
findings.body: LastOrDefault(l => l.Elevation <= z) does not select the nearest level below z unless the supplied list happens to be sorted by ascending elevation; the fallback FirstOrDefault likewise does not reliably select the lowest level. Revit collector/list ordering is not guaranteed by this constructor contract, so a foundation can silently be associated with the wrong level. Select the matching candidate explicitly by elevation (maximum elevation at or below z, with a deterministic nearest-level fallback).
